authority: Parliament of India / Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution

sources.title: Definition of Consumer
sources.summary: Defines a consumer as any person who buys goods or hires services for consideration, including offline or online transactions, electronic means, teleshopping, direct selling, or multi-level marketing, excluding goods bought for commercial purposes.

sources.title: Unfair Contract
sources.summary: Defines an unfair contract between a manufacturer or trader or service provider on one hand, and a consumer on the other, having terms which cause significant change in consumer rights, such as requiring excessive security deposits, imposing disproportionate penalty, refusing early payment, unilateral termination without reasonable cause, or assigning contract to detriment of consumer without consent.

sources.title: Unfair Trade Practice
sources.summary: Prohibits deceptive trade practices including false representations regarding standard, quality, or grade, misleading warranties or guarantees, non-issuance of tax invoice/cash memo, and refusing to take back defective goods or refund consideration paid within specified time.

sources.title: Jurisdiction of Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions
sources.summary: Establishes a three-tier quasi-judicial redressal mechanism: District Commission (claims up to INR 50 Lakhs), State Commission (claims exceeding INR 50 Lakhs up to INR 2 Crores), and National Commission (claims exceeding INR 2 Crores). Consumers can file complaints where they reside or work (e-Daakhil portal).

sources.title: Product Liability
sources.summary: A product manufacturer, product service provider, or product seller is liable to compensate a consumer for any harm caused by a defective product or deficiency in services.
